label: Step Label
title: Step Label
summary: Use a Step Label to keep a Step’s title, detail and date when you put your own content, such as a button, inside the Step.
corePrinciple: The stage in words: its name, one line of detail, and when.

content.title: A stage name, one line of detail, and a date
content.description: Write the title as the stage in one to four words, in sentence case, such as “Verify PAN”. Keep the supporting text to one line on what happens or what went wrong, and start the date with what it marks: Done, Started, or Due by.

sources.title: Use the public Step Label contract
sources.description: The guide compares Step’s text frame in Figma with the installed package and its Storybook stories.
blocks: Step’s text frame, in Coin Subcomponents

Installed jfs-components is 0.1.78 (27 October build) from the team’s private package repository. Figma has no Step Label component: it is the text frame inside Step in Coin Subcomponents, whose title, supporting text, and Meta text and subtitle and meta switches match the props. Only Color Mode, and AppearanceBrand for the supporting line, change the label, and it takes modes from its own prop, its Step, or JFSThemeProvider. It has no role or name of its own: the Step around it is announced by the label’s title, supporting text of up to 80 characters, and date, and the Step’s own title is ignored. Figma’s done example shows a green date; the package keeps it grey. The published Storybook predates 0.1.78.
